reasoning: Governing checks at worst case (load 2750 N, thickness minus 0.5 mm): bending stress 6PL/(b h^2) must stay under the ultimate allowable (ultimate/1.6) because it is tighter than yield/1.25, and tip deflection 4PL^3/(E b h^3) must stay under 3 mm. Thickness must be a stock value and satisfy t/b <= 2, so width is set by the larger of the stress, stiffness, and aspect-ratio limits. Rough sizing gives Ti-6Al-4V at about 20 mm x 12 mm (about 0.15 kg), Al 6061-T6 at about 30 mm x 15 mm (about 0.17 kg), and Steel 4130 at about 25 mm x 12.5 mm (about 0.34 kg). The specialists should verify these and check for better stock combinations.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Allowable is governed by ultimate: 310/1.6 = 194 MPa, with b*h^2 >= about 11,900 mm^3 at the worst case. Because E is only 68.9 GPa, the 3 mm deflection limit is also active, and t/b <= 2 pushes the search toward t=30 mm, b about 15 mm (about 450 mm^2, about 0.17 kg).
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Ultimate allowable 950/1.6 = 594 MPa is lower than yield 880/1.25 = 704 MPa, so stress is less limiting; stiffness governs with E = 113.8 GPa. Search t=20 mm with b about 12 mm (about 240 mm^2, about 0.15 kg), which is the lightest candidate, and check t=16 and t=25 nearby.
notes.Steel 4130: Yield governs at 435/1.25 = 348 MPa, requiring b*h^2 >= about 6,640 mm^3. The high E = 205 GPa makes stiffness easy, so search t=25 mm with b about 12.5 mm (about 312 mm^2, about 0.34 kg) and t=20 mm with b about 17.5 mm, expecting it to be the heaviest option.

attacks.title: REQ-006 combined case: load +10%, plate 0.5 mm thinner
attacks.rationale: Stress test confirms REQ-006 passes: yield MS 0.39, ultimate MS 0.17, deflection 2.981 mm vs 3.0 mm limit. Passes, but deflection margin is only 0.6%.

attacks.title: Machining loss: 1.0 mm off thickness (19 mm)
attacks.rationale: Survives: yield MS 0.45, ultimate MS 0.23, deflection 2.93 mm. Resulting 19 mm is not a stock size (REQ-005), so the part would need to be re-stocked or the finished thickness controlled.

attacks.title: Layout change: arm 10 mm longer (150 mm)
attacks.rationale: Fails REQ-003: deflection 3.09 mm vs 3.0 mm limit. Stress is fine (yield MS 0.50). Deflection scales with L^3, so a 7% longer arm adds about 23% deflection.

attacks.title: Launch or handling overload: 1.5x load
attacks.rationale: Fails REQ-002 and REQ-003: ultimate MS -0.095, yield MS 0.07 (passes only just), deflection 3.77 mm vs 3.0 mm limit. Overload from launch shock or handling is plausible.

attacks.title: Edge trim: 1 mm off width (11 mm)
attacks.rationale: Survives: deflection 2.74 mm, yield MS 0.48. Width loss hurts stiffness, not strength. At 2 mm lost (10 mm wide), t/w = 2.0 reaches the REQ-007 limit.

rationale: The team's 12 x 20 mm, 149 g design is not releasable because G-04 confirmed two attacks: a 150 mm arm pushes tip deflection to about 3.09 mm, above the 3 mm limit of REQ-003, and a 1.5x launch overload gives an ultimate margin of about -0.10, while G-02 shows the part only survives about 1.19x load. G-01 and G-03 pass, so the problem is geometry and margin rather than scatter, and another round can fix it within the envelope.

summary: The engine reports all structural checks passing (S-01 to S-04, S-06) and the bare-metal material, finish and cost checks passing (M-02, M-03, M-04, F-01 to F-03), but the bracket still relies on typical handbook allowables (M-01), unanalyzed fatigue (X-02) and an open galvanic-corrosion action at the joint (M-05). Fracture control classification (X-01) and the supplier, traceability and quality actions (P-01 to P-03) remain open, so the review should not be treated as release-ready.
top_risks: Fatigue is not analyzed, so launch vibration and other cyclic loads are unassessed (X-02).
Strength margins rest on typical handbook values rather than MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for this alloy, temper and thickness (M-01).
Galvanic corrosion at the Ti-6Al-4V joint is unresolved until fastener material and finish are specified (M-05).

actions.action: Replace typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V in the specified temper and 12 x 20 mm section, then rerun S-01 to S-03.
Define cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and complete the fatigue analysis.
Specify fastener material and finish for the joint to prevent galvanic corrosion under MIL-STD-889.
Classify the part (for example non-fracture-critical) and record the rationale.
Confirm the melt source is from the US or a qualifying country under DFARS 252.225-7009 before ordering.
